defects.class: dangling cached pointer released or used again (double free / use-after-free)
defects.description: rsa_ossl_finish released pinfo->m and rsa->_method_mod_{n,p,q} but left the freed pointers in those slots. RSA_set_method invokes the outgoing method's finish on every method transition and then installs the new table, so a second RSA_set_method released the same blocks again; alternatively the next private operation's BN_MONT_CTX_set_locked returned the dangling pointer from its non-NULL fast path and used it as a Montgomery context. The authority (rsa_ossl.c:1179-1195) has the same UB; AGENTS.md section 17 forbids reproducing it.
defects.fix: Clear every released slot (extra-prime pinfo->m and the three _method_mod_* fields) at its single release. Recorded at the function as a deliberate divergence; the difference is observable only to a caller that uses a released context. Added the_finish_hook_clears_every_slot_it_releases, which also acts as the double-release negative control.

defects.class: unchecked signed-to-unsigned allocation width (debug-build overflow across the C ABI)
defects.description: srp_Calc_xy computed numN = bn_num_bytes(N) and then cast it to usize and doubled it for the two-block scratch allocation. A live BIGNUM whose bit length overflowed the authority's int yields a negative width; the cast produces a huge usize and the doubling overflows, panicking a debug build across SRP_Calc_u_ex / SRP_Calc_u's extern "C" boundary. The authority's own allocation fails in that case.
defects.fix: Refuse a negative width by returning NULL after releasing the fetched digest, which is the authority's allocation-failure answer; the positive path is unchanged. Also narrowed srp_Calc_xy's contract: N is live because BN_num_bytes reads it, while x and y remain NULL-or-live (BN_ucmp accepts NULL).

residuals: slh_dsa_key_equal uses CRYPTO_memcmp for the public component where the authority uses memcmp; equality results are identical and the widening is constant-time on public data, so it is retained.

srp_Calc_xy continues to accept NULL x/y, which the authority's BN_ucmp tolerates as less-than; N is now documented live because the authority's BN_num_bytes macro dereferences it.
Line coordinates remain the crate's established convention; no CRYPTO_* seam coordinate was changed in this batch.
